sources.title: Yield visibility, censorship and kernel-mode formal boundary checks
sources.citation: crypto repository, research/ic_yield_rank_frontier_20261118 and two Lean owner modules (2026-11-18)
sources.notes: Kernel-checked generic theorems/countermodels plus a synthetic-only fixed-population schema and an 11-claim kernel-mode source audit. No natural population or asymptotic law is claimed.

nodes.label: Solver-visible yield is at most mathematical yield; completeness gives equality (Lean)
nodes.statement: For a finite decomposition map and any solver/filter predicate, the visible fibre is a subset of the mathematical fibre, so visible yield is at most mathematical yield target by target. Pointwise completeness makes the two fibres equal.
nodes.scope: Finite semantic map with a sound filtering interpretation. Does not prove that a production algebraic solver is sound or complete.

formal.notes: Lean 4.34.1 full build, axiom audit and repository proof gate passed locally.

nodes.label: 'Equal conserved mean determines target-wise yield shape'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: two decomposition maps with the same domain and codomain sizes, hence the same conserved mean, must have the same coverage, zero mass or target-wise counts.
nodes.scope: Refuted by two maps Bool -> Bool with equal total yield and different coverage/fibres.

nodes.label: Equal total yield, different coverage and fibres (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: The constant-false and identity maps Bool -> Bool both have total yield 2, but their coverage is 1 versus 2 and their yield at true is 0 versus 1.
nodes.scope: Finite implication countermodel only; not a model of a natural elliptic-curve factor base.

nodes.label: 'Mathematical decomposition yield automatically equals solver-visible yield'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: without a completeness hypothesis, a production solver/filter exposes every mathematical decomposition.
nodes.scope: Refuted by a reject-all filter on the Boolean identity map; production solvers require separate soundness/completeness evidence.

nodes.label: Reject-all solver hides a real decomposition (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: For the identity map on Bool, false has mathematical yield 1 while a reject-all solver/filter reports visible yield 0.
nodes.scope: Completeness implication countermodel only; it does not assert that a named solver rejects all witnesses.

nodes.label: 'Success-only retention preserves the failure distribution'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: a population obtained by retaining successful outcomes only can still establish the original failure mass.
nodes.scope: Refuted by the complete Boolean population; it motivates retention of every terminal outcome.

nodes.label: Success-only selection erases a real failure (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: The complete Boolean population has one failure, while filtering to successes leaves zero observed failures.
nodes.scope: Finite selection countermodel; it does not quantify the bias of a named adaptive stopping rule.

nodes.label: An unused relation column gives a nonzero right-kernel vector (Lean)
nodes.statement: Over any field, if one column of a finite relation matrix is zero in every row, its coordinate vector is a nonzero right-kernel vector; reusable full-column-rank recovery is impossible.
nodes.scope: Exact support obstruction; it does not assert that a natural population has an unused column.

formal.notes: Lean 4.34.1 full build, axiom audit and repository proof gate passed locally.

nodes.label: 'More rows than columns implies reusable full-column rank'
nodes.statement: Overbroad bridge: an n-by-B relation matrix with n>B has trivial right kernel and therefore uniquely determines a reusable factor-base table.
nodes.scope: Refuted by the zero matrix; row surplus does guarantee a nonzero left kernel, a different condition.

nodes.label: Row surplus with nonzero left and right kernels (Lean countermodel)
nodes.statement: For every B>0 over a field, the (B+1)-by-B zero matrix has a nonzero left-kernel vector by the existing theorem and an explicit nonzero right-kernel vector.
nodes.scope: Implication countermodel only; no claim that natural relation matrices are zero.

nodes.label: Two-summand relation-graph first-cycle law
nodes.statement: Prove or measure without stopping bias the law that the two-summand relation graph closes an eliminable cycle after about K/2 accepted edges under the route's exact vertex/edge process.
nodes.scope: Graph-cycle elimination mode; distinct from left-kernel existence and reusable right/full-rank tables.

edges.statement: Equal conserved totals coexist with different coverage and target fibres.
A target-wise law needs hypotheses beyond the conserved mean.
Coverage can change while the mean is fixed.
Visible yield is bounded above by mathematical yield and equals it only with a completeness certificate.
A reject-all filter hides an existing witness.
Mathematical enumeration alone cannot certify production-solver completeness.
Success-only filtering erases the failure mass.
A complete terminal manifest is necessary to distinguish zero, failure and rejection.
An unused column is an exact obstruction to reusable full-column rank.
Terminal rank requires support of every reusable column, not only a row surplus.
A surplus-row matrix can have nonzero left and right kernels simultaneously.
Row count alone does not discharge the reusable rank heuristic.
Left-kernel existence and right-kernel uniqueness are distinct obligations.
The family law uses first-cycle closure rather than a reusable full-rank table.
